land.text: the royal domain round Chengzhou (Luoyang) that the Zhou court kept after leaving Haojing

predecessors.note: Cliopatria splits the Zhou line at 750; the zhou-dynasty dossier ends at 751 with a dissolve to this slug. The page dates the move to 770 (Shiji) or 738 (Xinian); one state, one colour (master-plan rule 2) - a reviewer may merge the two files.

land.text: Wangcheng and Chengzhou, the last royal land, conquered by Qin in 256

successors.note: Qin took Wangcheng in 256 ('King Nan travelled to Xianyang to submit'); the East Zhou remnant was 'defeated in 251 and 249 BC' and 'annexed by Qin' (King Nan page, year of the annexation not on the page).

capitals.name: Chengzhou (Luoyi, near Luoyang)
capitals.note: Lead: 'the royal court's relocation eastward from Fenghao to Chengzhou (near present-day Luoyang)'; infobox capital Chengzhou. King Ping 'moved the capital east to Luoyi' (the page gives the Shiji's 770, the Xinian's later date).

capitals.name: Wangcheng (Luoyang)
capitals.note: 'At the beginning of his reign in 314 BC, King Nan moved the capital from Chengzhou to Wangcheng.' Coordinates are those of Luoyang's old city; the page does not give them.

rulers.name: King Ping of Zhou (Ji Yijiu)
rulers.title: King
rulers.note: The page gives 772-720; the move east is dated 770 (Shiji). A rival King Xie is given '770-760 or 771-750' and is not listed.

correction.text: for 635-451: the royal domain without Henei and Yangfan, which King Xiang gave to Duke Wen of Jin; as drawn for 750-636

keyframe_review.note: 9,654 km2 for 750-451, 46 cells with 18 of them north of the Yellow River (112.4-113.4 E, 34.9-35.4 N). The page gives no royal-domain extent, but dates the loss of Henei and Yangfan: Duke Wen of Jin 'killed Prince Dai and was rewarded with rule over Henei and Yangfan' (Chaos of Prince Dai, 635). The Spring and Autumn period page adds 'the king awarded Jin with strategically valuable territory near Chengzhou' (635). The shape stands for 750-636; from 635 it loses the Henei-Yangfan side (radius 40 km around 112.6 E, 35.1 N, the researcher's placing of Yangfan at Jiyuan).

correction.text: the royal domain round Chengzhou, 'near present-day Luoyang'

keyframe_review.note: 6,027 km2 for 450-405 (27 cells, 112.1-113.5 E, 34.9-35.4 N). The shape does not contain Luoyang: 0 of 10 cells within 25 km of Luoyang, while the page puts the capital at 'Chengzhou (near present-day Luoyang)' and the pages keep the court there to 256. Cliopatria moves the Luoyang strip (15 cells to Jin, 4 to Chu) out of the Zhou shape in 450; no page opened supports that, and the Henei side that the shape keeps is the land given to Jin in 635. Corrected to a 35 km disc around Luoyang (about 3,800 km2); the page has no area to compare.

correction.text: the royal domain round Chengzhou, 'near present-day Luoyang'

keyframe_review.note: 6,327 km2 for 404-367, same outline as 450-405 (0 of 10 Luoyang cells). Same correction: the court sat at Chengzhou near Luoyang.

correction.text: the royal domain round Chengzhou, 'near present-day Luoyang'

keyframe_review.note: 5,929 km2 for 366-351 (2 cells to Han in Cliopatria, page silent). Same correction: the capital area is missing from the shape. The royal land 'was split into two states or factions' (undated on the page).

correction.text: Chengzhou, Wangcheng and the royal seat at Luoyang, the last Zhou land

keyframe_review.note: 3,966 km2 for 350-257 (17 cells, 112.2-113.5 E, 35.1-35.5 N), 9 cells fewer than 366 (to Han in Cliopatria, page silent). The shape lacks Wangcheng and Chengzhou, both at Luoyang (0 of 10 cells): 'King Nan moved the capital from Chengzhou to Wangcheng' in 314, and Qin 'finally conquered' Wangcheng in 256. Corrected to the Luoyang disc; the page says the king 'lacked any personal territory', so the extent is the court's seat, soft.

region.text: the Zhou court at Chengzhou after the move east

ledger.note: 770: the Zhou court moves east and the Eastern Zhou begins. 'According to traditional historical texts such as the Records of the Grand Historian, the Zhou capital was moved from Haojing' (770); 'In the second year of his reign, he moved the capital east to Luoyi as Quanrong people invaded Haojing'; the Xinian places the move three years after King Ping's enthronement (738). Cliopatria begins this shape at 750.

635: King Xiang rewards Duke Wen of Jin with Henei and Yangfan. In the Chaos of Prince Dai paragraph, Duke Wen of Jin 'killed Prince Dai and was rewarded with rule over Henei and Yangfan'. The paragraph's year is 635; the sentence has no year of its own. The Spring and Autumn period page: 'the king awarded Jin with strategically valuable territory near Chengzhou' (635). Place of Yangfan (Jiyuan) is the researcher's.
314: King Nan moves the capital from Chengzhou to Wangcheng. 'At the beginning of his reign in 314 BC, King Nan moved the capital from Chengzhou to Wangcheng.'

region.text: East Zhou, 'centered at Chengzhou and Kung'; West Zhou kept Wangcheng

ledger.note: By 314 the royal land is two states. 'even their remaining crown land was split into two states, led by rival feudal lords'; West Zhou's capital is Wangcheng, East Zhou 'centered at Chengzhou and Kung'. Page silent on the year of the split (the 314 capital move shows it had happened); the researcher places Gong at 112.98 E, 34.77 N.

region.text: Wangcheng and the last royal land

ledger.note: 256: Qin conquers Wangcheng. 'Wangcheng was finally conquered in 256 BC, and King Nan travelled to Xianyang to submit to King Zhaoxiang of Qin'; 'Qin seized the Nine Tripod Cauldrons and exiled Nan's heir, Ji Wen, to Danhu'; infobox 'Died: 256 BC'. The Qin page's table: '256 BC Qin ended the Eastern Zhou dynasty'.

region.text: the last Zhou land, Wangcheng and Chengzhou

ledger.note: 256: the Zhou kings end. 'Imprisoned in Wangcheng, he died shortly afterwards, "and the rituals of the Zhou dynasty ceased forever"'; the Eastern Zhou page: 'his deposition and execution by Qin in 256 BC'. The East Zhou remnant 'was defeated in 251 and 249 BC' and 'annexed by Qin' (year of the annexation not on the page); this dossier ends at the king's death.

wars.name: Battle of Xuge
wars.outcome: Zheng defeated the royal forces; the king's authority never recovered.
wars.note: 'defeating the royal forces in the Battle of Xuge' (707); no land changed hands.

wars.name: Rebellion of Prince Dai
wars.outcome: Duke Wen of Jin killed Prince Dai and was rewarded with Henei and Yangfan.
wars.note: Only the paragraph's year (635) is on the page.

wars.name: Qin conquest of the Zhou
wars.outcome: Qin conquered Wangcheng and took the Nine Tripod Cauldrons; King Nan submitted and died; the East Zhou remnant fell in 249.
wars.note: 'Qin to invade Zhou and end their line of monarchs in 256 BC' (Warring States period page); King Zhaoxiang of Qin: 'overthrew the Eastern Zhou dynasty in 256 BC'.

certainty.note: No source gives the royal domain's boundaries; the drawn disc around Chengzhou is the seat, not a frontier.
The land was split between West Zhou at Wangcheng and East Zhou at Chengzhou and Gong, and the king 'lacked any personal territory'.

notes: Cliopatria row 'Later Zhou' (-750..960) is split here: the five shapes -750..-257 are the Eastern Zhou royal domain (this dossier, slug eastern-zhou = slugify of the name, cliopatria_names ['Later Zhou']); the single 960 shape is the Five Dynasties Later Zhou, written as its own dossier 'later-zhou'. The validator will warn here that 'later-zhou_960' has no verdict; it is reviewed in later-zhou.json. The Wikidata id Q1154556 belongs to the Five Dynasties dynasty, so this dossier has wikidata null. Big finding: Cliopatria's Zhou shapes from 450 on do not contain Luoyang (0 of 10 cells within 25 km), the royal capital, and sit on the Henei side north of the Yellow River, which the pages say Jin received in 635; Cliopatria gives the Luoyang strip to Jin (15 cells) and Chu (4) in 450. All four shapes are corrected to a Luoyang disc. Not dated by any page opened: the split into East and West Zhou (Shiji date not on the Eastern Zhou, King Nan or Warring States pages), the 366 and 350 losses of 2 and 9 cells to Han, and the 4-cell Chu strip of 450. Needs a dossier: 'east-zhou', the statelet of the Duke of Eastern Zhou, to 249 (counterparts_needing_dossiers). Vassalage: the states of the Spring and Autumn period are not recorded as Zhou vassals here; the Cliopatria umbrellas (Spring and Autumn States, Warring States China) are the association and the zhou-dynasty dossier ends the nominal tint at 751. Budget: 4 pages (the shape count would have allowed 5). Region names: 'Luoyang' is in the gazetteer; 'Wangcheng', 'Chengzhou' and 'Gong' are not (coordinates used); gazetteer_names_needed: Chengzhou, Wangcheng, Gong, Yangfan.
